digest.lead: A quiet news day: Claude Code shipped another incremental patch closing security gaps around worktree isolation and hook permissions, while Anthropic announced a new addition to its leadership or advisory ranks with Tino Cuellar.
digest.summary: No major model releases or product launches today — coverage centers on a routine Claude Code changelog update and an Anthropic personnel announcement.

stories.headline: Anthropic Announces Tino Cuellar
stories.summary: Anthropic published a brief announcement regarding Tino Cuellar [1]. Details of the specific role or capacity were not elaborated in the source content.
stories.impact: Leadership and advisory additions can signal Anthropic's priorities around governance, policy, or safety as it scales — relevant to enterprises and policymakers tracking Anthropic's institutional direction.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.222 Patches Git Isolation and Hook Permission Bypass
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release fixes a bug that allowed worktree-isolated sessions and their subagents to run destructive git commands against the main checkout, extending isolation to file edits and Bash across all session types [1]. It also closes a gap where PreToolUse auto-allow hooks could bypass tool restrictions during background agent tasks like summaries, compaction, and renames, and fixes a Team/Enterprise `/usage-credits` bug that blocked members from resubmitting dismissed credit requests [1].
key_points: Worktree isolation now covers file edits and Bash commands in every session type, preventing subagents from affecting the main checkout [1].
Background agent tasks (summaries, compaction, renames) can no longer bypass tool restrictions via auto-allow hooks [1].
Team/Enterprise usage-credit requests are no longer blocked after an earlier request was dismissed [1].
stories.impact: Teams running Claude Code with git worktrees or custom hook-based permission restrictions get meaningfully tighter security guarantees, reducing risk of destructive operations leaking outside isolated sessions.

stories.headline: Configure MCP servers with the right installation scope
stories.summary: Claude Code supports local, project, and user scopes for MCP server configuration, which determines whether a server connection is available just to you, shared with your team via the repo, or available across all your projects. Choosing the correct scope avoids leaking credentials into shared config or missing servers you need in other projects.
actionable_steps: Use local scope for personal, one-off server connections you don't want to share
Use project scope (checked into .mcp.json) for servers your whole team should access
Use user scope for servers you want available across all your own projects
Use environment variable expansion in .mcp.json to avoid hardcoding secrets like API keys

stories.headline: Set up hooks to automate Claude Code workflows at key events
stories.summary: Hooks allow you to run custom scripts or commands automatically when specific events occur in Claude Code, such as session start, prompt submission, or instruction loading. This enables automated setup, validation, or custom integrations.
actionable_steps: Create hook configuration files in your project's .claude directory
Define hook events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, etc.) and their corresponding actions
Configure hook handlers with command, HTTP, or MCP tool fields as needed
Test hooks using the /hooks menu to verify they trigger correctly

stories.headline: Enable feedback surveys for enterprise OpenTelemetry users
stories.summary: If your enterprise captures telemetry data through OpenTelemetry, you can now re-enable Claude Code's session quality surveys to gather user feedback. This helps organizations collect structured feedback data alongside their existing telemetry infrastructure.
actionable_steps: Verify that session quality surveys now appear in your Claude Code interface

stories.headline: Use safe-mode flag to troubleshoot Claude Code issues
stories.summary: When Claude Code behaves unexpectedly, safe mode disables all customizations including CLAUDE.md files, plugins, skills, hooks, and MCP servers. This helps isolate whether issues stem from your configurations or the base application.
actionable_steps: Test if your issue persists in safe mode
If the issue disappears, gradually re-enable customizations to identify the culprit

stories.headline: Set language setting to control session title generation
stories.summary: Claude Code now generates session titles in the language of your conversation. You can pin a specific language to ensure consistent title generation regardless of conversation content.
actionable_steps: Set it to your preferred language code (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr')
